lesson.subtitle: Lesson 15 -- On a Call -- Clarifying
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Thiago Negrães | Lesson 15 -- On a Call
lesson.grammar_point: indirect questions for clarifying (could you tell me, do you know, I'd like to know if)

listenings.text: I coach engineers who work with teams in other countries, and here is the first thing I tell them. Most problems on international calls are not about English. They are about silence. Somebody does not catch a number, and instead of asking, they say nothing and hope it comes back later. It never does. So ask, and ask early. You do not need a perfect sentence. Sorry, I didn't catch that is enough. If you want to sound more professional, put a polite start in front of your question: could you tell me what the deadline is, do you know if the client approved it. And at the end of every call, take one minute to repeat the action items. It feels slow, but it saves a week of emails.

Hi Thiago, this is Mark from the Houston office. I am calling to follow up on the pumping station. Rachel told me the client wants a higher capacity, and I would like to know if that changes the budget. Could you also tell me when you can send the new specification? The client meeting is on Tuesday, so Monday morning would be ideal. One more thing. I am not sure what the new flow rate is, so please double-check it with your team before you send anything. Call me back when you can, or send me an email. Thanks, and have a good weekend.

extra_audio.text: First, Rachel says she wants to go over the pumping station. Then, Thiago asks her to repeat, because he did not catch the last part. After that, Rachel explains that the client changed the capacity. Next, Thiago asks what the new flow rate is, and Rachel says she needs to double-check. Finally, Rachel promises an email with the action items.

items.situation: On a call, you did not hear the last number.
tips: Start with sorry and the verb catch.
Then ask the person to say it again.

items.situation: You want to know the new deadline, politely.
tips: Start with Could you tell me...
Then the deadline and the verb is, at the end.

items.situation: You are not sure if the client approved the design.
tips: No does or did after if: the client approved it.

items.situation: Your colleague says something very complicated.
tips: Ask the person to explain it more simply.
There is a phrasal verb with spell.

items.situation: The call is ending and you want everybody to agree on the next steps.
tips: Use the expression for the tasks after a meeting.
Finish with: so we are on the same page.
